title: Project brief, business case and the benefits and sustainability approaches
blurb: Explain the purpose of the project brief, business case, benefits management approach and sustainability management approach, and when each is created and used.
question: A project manager needs a product that defines how benefits will be measured and reviewed after the project closes. Which management product is it, and when is it created?

teach.body: Formally: the project brief provides a full and firm foundation for initiating the project; the business case documents the business justification, based on estimated costs against expected benefits, offset by associated risks; the benefits management approach defines the benefits management actions and reviews; and the sustainability management approach defines the actions, reviews and controls for sustainability targets. In plain English: a launch pad, the argument, a plan to prove the gains, and a plan to hit the green targets.

teach.caption: SU = starting up a project; IP = initiating a project; SB = managing a stage boundary; CP = closing a project.

teach.body: The project brief is assembled in starting up a project and gives a full and firm foundation for initiation. It brings together, among other things, the outline business case and the project approach. The board reviews it when authorizing initiation, and it is superseded by the PID. On a small, low-value project, the brief and business case may be merged into one simple business case document.

The business case documents the justification: estimated costs against expected benefits, offset by risks. Key headings include reasons (why the project is needed and how it enables business objectives), expected benefits (measurable, against the situation before the project), time (how long the project runs and the period over which benefits are realized) and costs (project costs plus ongoing operations and maintenance costs and how they are funded).

teach.body: The benefits management approach defines the benefits management actions and benefits reviews needed to ensure the outcomes are achieved and to confirm the benefits are realized, including benefits tolerance, measures, timing and responsibilities. The sustainability management approach defines the actions, reviews and controls to ensure the sustainability performance targets are achieved; it supports the business case and references ESG goals. Both are agreed in initiation.

teach.h: Which product does this belong in?

teach.body: Tidewell Credit Union is building a mobile app. In starting up, project manager Aisha Rahman assembles the project brief with an outline business case. In initiation she prepares the full business case: reasons (members moving to app-only banks), expected benefits (20% fewer branch transactions), time (9 months, benefits over 3 years) and costs (including annual support). The benefits management approach sets reviews at 6 and 18 months; the sustainability management approach targets lower server energy use.

teach.text: Classic traps: the project brief belongs to starting up and is superseded by the PID, which is assembled in initiation. The business case states the expected benefits; the benefits management approach says how and when they will be measured and reviewed. Post-project benefits reviews are planned in the benefits management approach, not carried out by the project.

items: Project brief: full and firm foundation for initiation; starting up; superseded by the PID.
Business case: justification from costs against benefits, offset by risks.
Business case headings include reasons, expected benefits, time and costs.
Benefits management approach: benefits actions and reviews; created in initiation, updated SB and CP.
Sustainability management approach: actions, reviews and controls for sustainability targets.

summary: You can now state the purpose of the project brief, business case, benefits management approach and sustainability management approach. You can also say when each is created and updated, and which business case heading a piece of information belongs under.

A.q: What is the purpose of the project brief?
options: To document the business justification for the project
To define the benefits management actions and reviews
To provide a full and firm foundation for initiation
To give the direction and scope of the whole project
A.why: The project brief provides a full and firm foundation for the initiation of the project (manual 5.5).

whyNot.0: Documenting the business justification is the purpose of the business case.
whyNot.1: This is the purpose of the benefits management approach.
whyNot.3: This is the purpose of the PID.

A.q: Which product documents the business justification for the project, based on estimated costs against expected benefits, offset by associated risks?
options: Business case
Project brief
Benefits management approach
Project plan
A.why: The business case documents the business justification: costs against benefits, offset by risks (manual 5.5).

whyNot.1: The project brief is the foundation for initiation; it contains the outline business case.
whyNot.2: The benefits management approach defines how benefits will be managed and reviewed.
whyNot.3: The project plan provides time and cost estimates that feed the business case.

A.q: What does the benefits management approach define?
options: Sustainability actions, reviews and controls
Costs set against expected benefits and risks
The foundation needed to initiate the project
Benefits management actions and benefits reviews
A.why: It defines the benefits management actions and benefits reviews that ensure outcomes are achieved and confirm benefits are realized (manual 5.5).

whyNot.0: This is the sustainability management approach.

B.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. The project brief is superseded by the PID.
2. The sustainability management approach is created in starting up a project.
3. The benefits management approach is updated in closing a project to plan post-project reviews.
4. The business case 'time' heading covers the project's duration but not the benefits period.
options: 1 and 2
2 and 4
1 and 3
3 and 4
B.why: The PID supersedes the project brief (1), and closing a project updates the benefits management approach for post-project reviews (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: the management approaches are agreed in initiation.
whyNot.1: Both are false: the approach is created in initiation, and 'time' covers the benefits period too.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: 'time' covers both the project period and the period over which benefits are realized.

B.q: Under which business case heading should the ongoing maintenance costs of a new system and their funding arrangements be recorded?
options: Expected benefits
Costs
Reasons
Time
B.why: The costs heading summarizes project costs, ongoing operations and maintenance costs and their funding arrangements.

whyNot.0: Expected benefits are the measurable improvements against today's situation.
whyNot.2: Reasons explain why the project is needed.
whyNot.3: Time covers the project period and the benefits period.

B.q: A small, low-value project wants to keep its documentation light. Which tailoring of the business case products is appropriate?
options: Merge the project brief and business case into one
Drop the business case because the project is small
Let the project manager approve the business case
Combine the business case with the risk register
B.why: Small, low-value projects may merge the project brief and business case into one simple business case document (manual 5.4.5).

whyNot.1: Every project needs business justification; tailoring changes its format, not its existence.
whyNot.2: Approval stays with the board; the executive is accountable for the business case.
whyNot.3: The risk register is a project log record; merging it with the business case is not the recommended tailoring.

C.q: In which process is the project brief assembled, and which board activity approves it?
options: Initiating a project; authorize the project
Starting up a project; authorize the project
Initiating a project; authorize initiation
Starting up a project; authorize initiation
C.why: The project brief is assembled in starting up a project and approved by the board in authorize initiation.

whyNot.0: Initiation assembles the PID, which the board approves in authorize the project.
whyNot.1: The process is right, but the brief is approved in authorize initiation.
whyNot.2: The brief is assembled in starting up, before initiation begins.

C.q: A credit union's business case says the project will run for 9 months and benefits will be realized over 3 years. Under which heading is this recorded, and what does it cover?
options: Time: the project's stage dates and milestones
Time: the project period and the benefits period
Expected benefits: the measurable gains over time
Reasons: why the project needs nine months
C.why: The time heading covers the period over which the project runs and the period over which the benefits are realized.

whyNot.0: Right heading, but it covers the project and benefits periods, not stage dates.
whyNot.2: Expected benefits are the measurable improvements, not the time periods.
whyNot.3: Reasons explain why the project is needed, not how long it runs.

C.q: Which statement correctly contrasts the business case with the benefits management approach?
options: The business case states the benefits; the approach plans their reviews
The business case plans benefit reviews; the approach states the benefits
The business case starts in initiation; the approach in starting up
The senior user owns the business case; the PM owns the approach
C.why: The business case records the expected benefits; the benefits management approach defines the actions and reviews to confirm they are realized.

whyNot.2: The outline business case starts in starting up; the approach is agreed in initiation.
whyNot.3: The executive, not the senior user, is accountable for the business case, and the board approves the approaches.

reteach.title: Planning a charity bike ride
reteach.question: You are organizing a sponsored bike ride. Which papers would you need before committing money, and which after?

blocks.body: A one-page outline lets the committee agree to plan properly (project brief). A fuller paper sets out why, the money it will raise, how long it takes and what it costs (business case). A note says how and when you will count the money raised, even after the event (benefits management approach). Another sets a limit on waste and travel emissions (sustainability management approach).

blocks.text: The project brief is replaced by the PID once initiation is complete. The business case lives on and is updated every stage.

explain.body: Assembled in starting up as a full and firm foundation for initiation. Reviewed in authorize initiation and later superseded by the PID.

test.q: What happens to the project brief once the PID is assembled?
options: It becomes the first end stage report
It is handed to the business layer
It is updated at every stage end
It is superseded by the PID
test.why: The project brief is superseded by the PID assembled in initiation.

whyNot.0: End stage reports are produced at stage boundaries from current data.
whyNot.1: The brief stays within the project's management products; it is not handed over.
whyNot.2: The business case is updated each stage; the brief is replaced.

explain.body: Reasons explain why the project is needed and how it will help achieve business objectives.

test.q: A hospital's complaints have risen 40% in two years, which is why a project has been proposed. Under which business case heading should this be recorded?
options: Reasons
Expected benefits
Time
Costs
test.why: Reasons explain why the project is being undertaken; a rise in complaints is the reason for the project.

whyNot.1: Expected benefits would be the measurable improvement, such as fewer complaints.
whyNot.2: Time covers the project and benefits periods.
whyNot.3: Costs summarize project and ongoing costs and their funding.

explain.body: Agreed in initiation with the other management approaches; reviewed by the board when authorizing the project; updated at stage boundaries and in closing.

test.q: In which process is the benefits management approach created?
options: Starting up a project
Initiating a project
Closing a project
Managing a stage boundary
test.why: The benefits management approach is one of the management approaches agreed in initiating a project.

whyNot.0: Starting up produces the project brief and outline business case.
whyNot.2: Closing a project updates it to plan post-project reviews.
whyNot.3: Stage boundaries update it with the results of benefits actions.

explain.body: Defines the actions, reviews and controls to achieve the sustainability performance targets. It supports the business case and references ESG goals.

test.q: Which product supports the business case by defining the actions, reviews and controls for sustainability performance targets?
options: Benefits management approach
Quality management approach
Sustainability management approach
Digital and data management approach
test.why: The sustainability management approach defines the actions, reviews and controls for sustainability performance targets and supports the business case.

whyNot.0: The benefits management approach covers benefits actions and reviews.
whyNot.1: The quality management approach covers how quality will be achieved.
whyNot.3: The digital and data management approach covers how data and information will be handled.
